key_insight: A spectral interface-evolution model shows that in rough fractures, viscosity mainly changes how fast Haines jumps relax, not the total energy dissipated between metastable states.
engineering_relevance: This gives a computationally efficient way to predict hysteresis and dissipation in fractured or porous media, supporting better upscaling for flow-control and transport design.
method: Spectral computational approach for tracking fluid-fluid interface evolution in a variable-aperture Hele-Shaw cell
Energy-dissipation calculation across quasistatic and finite-rate driving
Validated against CFD simulations and experiments, then applied to single-defect and random-roughness cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by comparison to CFD simulations and experiments, with demonstrations on a single defect and random roughness over many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach is designed for a simplified model fracture, so extension to fully 3D, strongly coupled porous-media geometries may require additional modeling and validation.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
